description: An in-depth study of how data is transmitted between devices, covering communication components, transmission modes and media, signals, modems, protocols, networking devices, and error checking.

mcq.questionText: Data communication is best defined as the process of:

options.text: Storing data permanently on a hard disk
Exchanging data between two or more devices through a transmission medium
Converting a program into machine code

mcq.explanation: Data communication is the exchange (transfer) of data between two or more devices over a transmission medium, using an agreed protocol.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT one of the basic components of a data communication system?
mcq.explanation: The five basic components are the sender, message, transmission medium, receiver and protocol. A power supply unit is not counted as a communication component.

mcq.questionText: In a data communication system, the set of rules that governs how data is exchanged is called the:
mcq.explanation: A protocol is a set of rules that both sender and receiver agree on so that communication is understood correctly.

mcq.questionText: A transmission mode in which data flows in only one direction, like a radio broadcast, is called:
mcq.explanation: In simplex mode data travels in one direction only; the receiver cannot send back. Radio and television broadcasts are examples.

mcq.questionText: Which transmission mode allows data to flow in both directions but only one direction at a time, as in a walkie-talkie?
mcq.explanation: Half-duplex allows two-way communication but not simultaneously; each side takes turns, like a walkie-talkie.

mcq.questionText: A telephone conversation, where both people can talk and listen at the same time, is an example of which transmission mode?
mcq.explanation: Full-duplex allows data to flow in both directions simultaneously, as in a normal telephone call.

mcq.questionText: In parallel transmission, data is sent:

options.text: One bit at a time over a single wire
Several bits at the same time over multiple wires

mcq.explanation: Parallel transmission sends multiple bits simultaneously, each on its own wire, making it faster over short distances but more costly.

mcq.questionText: Which statement correctly compares serial and parallel transmission?

options.text: Serial sends one bit at a time and is suited for long distances
Serial sends many bits at once over many wires
Parallel is cheaper for very long distances
Parallel can use only one wire

mcq.explanation: Serial transmission sends bits one after another on a single line, which is cheaper and more reliable over long distances; parallel uses many wires and suits short distances.

mcq.questionText: An analog signal is best described as one that:

options.text: Has only two discrete values, 0 and 1
Varies continuously over time, like a sound wave
Can only be stored on a computer

mcq.explanation: An analog signal is continuous and can take any value within a range, such as the human voice or a sound wave.

mcq.questionText: The full meaning of the word 'modem' comes from which two operations?
mcq.explanation: Modem stands for modulator-demodulator: it modulates digital data into analog for transmission and demodulates received analog signals back into digital.

mcq.questionText: Modulation in a modem refers to converting:
mcq.explanation: Modulation is the process of converting digital data from the computer into analog signals suitable for transmission over media such as telephone lines.

mcq.questionText: Bandwidth in data communication refers to:

options.text: The physical length of a cable
The maximum amount of data a channel can carry in a given time
The number of computers in a network
The colour of a network cable

mcq.explanation: Bandwidth is the capacity of a communication channel, often measured in bits per second (bps); higher bandwidth means more data can be carried.

mcq.questionText: Which transmission medium uses light to carry data and offers very high speed with immunity to electrical interference?
mcq.explanation: Fibre optic cable transmits data as pulses of light, giving very high bandwidth, long distance and immunity to electromagnetic interference.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an UNGUIDED (wireless) transmission medium?
mcq.explanation: Microwave is an unguided medium because it sends signals through the air without a physical cable; twisted pair, coaxial and fibre optic are guided media.

mcq.questionText: A parity bit is added to transmitted data mainly to:

options.text: Detect errors that occur during transmission

mcq.explanation: A parity bit is an extra bit added to make the number of 1s even or odd, allowing the receiver to detect single-bit errors in the data.

fib.questionText: The component of a data communication system that originates and sends the data is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The sender (source) is the device or person that generates and transmits the message.

fib.questionText: A transmission mode in which data flows in one direction only is called _____.
fib.explanation: Simplex transmission allows data to move in a single direction only, such as a radio or TV broadcast.

fib.questionText: In _____ transmission, bits are sent one after another along a single wire.
fib.explanation: Serial transmission sends one bit at a time over a single line, which is economical and reliable over long distances.

fib.questionText: A signal that has only two distinct states, represented as 0 and 1, is called a _____ signal.
fib.explanation: A digital signal is discrete, taking only specific values (such as 0 and 1), which computers use internally.

fib.questionText: The device that converts digital signals to analog for transmission and back again is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A modem (modulator-demodulator) modulates outgoing digital data into analog and demodulates incoming analog back into digital.

fib.questionText: The amount of data a communication channel can carry per unit of time is known as _____.
fib.explanation: Bandwidth measures the data-carrying capacity of a channel, commonly expressed in bits per second.

fib.questionText: The unit used to measure the data transfer rate of a communication channel is bits per _____.
fib.explanation: Data transfer rate is measured in bits per second (bps), which states how many bits travel through the channel each second.

fib.questionText: A networking device that joins different networks together and directs data along the best path is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A router connects different networks and forwards data packets between them using the best available route.

fib.questionText: The card fitted inside a computer that allows it to connect to a network is called a _____ (NIC).
fib.explanation: A Network Interface Card (NIC) provides the hardware connection that lets a computer communicate on a network.

fib.questionText: An extra bit added to data to check for errors during transmission is called a _____ bit.
fib.explanation: A parity bit is added so the receiver can check whether the number of 1s is correct and detect single-bit errors.

tf.questionText: A protocol is one of the basic components of a data communication system.
tf.explanation: True. The basic components are sender, message, medium, receiver and protocol; the protocol is the set of agreed rules.

tf.questionText: In full-duplex transmission, data can flow in both directions at the same time.
tf.explanation: True. Full-duplex allows simultaneous two-way communication, as in a telephone call.

tf.questionText: Parallel transmission is generally preferred over serial transmission for very long distances.
tf.explanation: False. Serial transmission is preferred for long distances because it is cheaper and more reliable; parallel suits short distances.

tf.questionText: A digital signal is continuous and can take any value within a range.
tf.explanation: False. A digital signal is discrete (e.g. 0 and 1); it is the analog signal that is continuous.

tf.questionText: Fibre optic cable is immune to electromagnetic interference because it transmits data as light.
tf.explanation: True. Since fibre optic carries data as pulses of light, it is not affected by electrical or electromagnetic interference.

tf.questionText: Bluetooth and Wi-Fi are examples of guided (wired) transmission media.
tf.explanation: False. Bluetooth and Wi-Fi are unguided (wireless) media because they send signals through the air without cables.

tf.questionText: Higher bandwidth generally allows more data to be transmitted in a given time.
tf.explanation: True. Bandwidth is the channel's capacity, so a higher bandwidth means a higher possible data transfer rate.

tf.questionText: TCP/IP is a set of protocols used for communication over the Internet.
tf.explanation: True. TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) is the standard suite of protocols that governs Internet communication.

tf.questionText: A switch and a hub are both used to connect devices within a network.
tf.explanation: True. Both connect devices in a local network; a switch forwards data only to the intended device, while a hub broadcasts to all ports.

tf.questionText: A parity bit can correct any error that occurs during transmission.
tf.explanation: False. A simple parity bit can only detect single-bit errors, not correct them; other techniques are needed for correction.

summary.questionText: List the five basic components of a data communication system.
summary.correctAnswer: Sender, message, transmission medium, receiver and protocol.
summary.explanation: Every data communication system needs a source (sender), the data being sent (message), a path (medium), a destination (receiver) and agreed rules (protocol).

summary.questionText: Name the three data transmission modes and give one example of each.
summary.correctAnswer: Simplex (radio/TV broadcast), half-duplex (walkie-talkie), and full-duplex (telephone call).
summary.explanation: Simplex is one-way, half-duplex is two-way one-at-a-time, and full-duplex is two-way simultaneously.

summary.questionText: State one advantage and one disadvantage of parallel transmission compared with serial transmission.
summary.correctAnswer: Advantage: it is faster over short distances because many bits are sent at once. Disadvantage: it is costly and unreliable over long distances because it needs many wires.
summary.explanation: Parallel uses multiple wires to send several bits simultaneously, gaining speed but losing economy and reliability over distance.

summary.questionText: Differentiate between an analog signal and a digital signal.
summary.correctAnswer: An analog signal varies continuously over a range of values (e.g. sound waves), while a digital signal is discrete with only fixed values such as 0 and 1.
summary.explanation: Analog is continuous; digital is discrete. Computers work with digital signals while many transmission lines originally carried analog.

summary.questionText: Explain the role of a modem in data communication.
summary.correctAnswer: A modem modulates digital data from a computer into analog signals for transmission and demodulates received analog signals back into digital data the computer can use.
summary.explanation: The modem (modulator-demodulator) allows digital computers to communicate over media that carry analog signals.

summary.correctAnswer: Twisted pair cable, coaxial cable and fibre optic cable.
summary.explanation: Guided media carry signals along a physical path; the three common types are twisted pair, coaxial and fibre optic.

summary.questionText: Give two advantages of fibre optic cable over copper cables.
summary.correctAnswer: It offers very high bandwidth/speed and is immune to electromagnetic interference; it also supports longer distances with less signal loss.
summary.explanation: Because data travels as light, fibre optic provides high capacity, immunity to interference and low attenuation over long distances.

summary.questionText: List four common data communication devices used in networks.
summary.correctAnswer: Router, switch, hub, network interface card (NIC), modem and wireless access point are examples (any four).
summary.explanation: These devices connect computers, direct traffic and provide access to networks; routers join networks, switches/hubs connect devices, NICs attach a computer, and access points provide wireless access.

summary.questionText: Explain how a parity bit is used to check for errors in transmission.
summary.correctAnswer: A parity bit is added to a group of bits to make the total number of 1s even (or odd); the receiver recalculates parity and, if it does not match, knows an error occurred.
summary.explanation: Parity checking detects single-bit errors by comparing the expected and received number of 1s.

summary.questionText: State four factors that affect data transmission.
summary.correctAnswer: Bandwidth of the channel, type of transmission medium, distance between devices, noise/interference, and the number of users sharing the channel (any four).
summary.explanation: These factors determine the speed and reliability of communication; greater bandwidth and better media improve performance while distance, noise and congestion reduce it.

hoq.questionText: A school wants to connect its computer laboratory to the Internet through an existing analog telephone line. Which device is essential to make this possible, and why?

options.text: A modem, because it converts the computer's digital signals to analog for the line and back again
A hub, because it broadcasts data to all telephones
A printer, because it produces a record of the data
A scanner, because it digitises documents

hoq.explanation: An analog telephone line cannot carry digital signals directly, so a modem is needed to modulate digital data into analog for sending and demodulate analog back into digital on receiving.

hoq.questionText: An engineer must lay a high-speed data link between two buildings that have heavy electrical machinery generating strong electromagnetic interference. Which transmission medium is the most suitable choice?

options.text: Twisted pair cable, because it is the cheapest option
Coaxial cable, because it is thick
Fibre optic cable, because it carries data as light and is immune to electromagnetic interference
Infrared, because it does not need cables

hoq.explanation: Fibre optic transmits data as light pulses, so electromagnetic interference from machinery does not affect it, and it also provides very high bandwidth for a high-speed link.

hoq.questionText: A walkie-talkie set lets two security guards talk to each other but only one can speak at a time. Which transmission mode does this illustrate, and what would have to change for them to speak simultaneously?

options.text: Simplex; it would need a longer antenna
Half-duplex; it would need to support full-duplex for simultaneous two-way communication
Simplex; it would need a parity bit

hoq.explanation: Taking turns to speak is half-duplex (two-way but not simultaneous); to talk and listen at the same time the system would need to operate in full-duplex mode.
